================================================================
PER-SUBSECTION PROMPT — SHARED PRELUDE
================================================================

**Concatenate with one of the 9 per-subsection delta files at invocation time.**

This prelude provides dissertation-specific context that the `/god-write` pipeline cannot derive from the corpus alone: §§1.0-1.4 inheritance, dissertation coinages, advisor-rigor blacklist, supplementary evidence pack (Sources A-E).

The pipeline's `--subsection-mode` flag handles output format (LaTeX `\subsubsection*{...}`), word target, quotation density, section structure, and most stylistic constraints automatically. This prelude does NOT duplicate those mandates.

================================================================
ARCHITECTURAL INHERITANCE FROM §§1.0–1.4
================================================================

The dissertation's overarching thesis: the soul is constitutively rhetorical, with *phantasia* as the temporal-kinetic medium that generates a continuous, affectively charged narrative of experience across past, present, and future.

The five-node actualization chain (established in §1.0):

- **A_0** — dyadic first actuality of sensible object + *aisthētikon* within the encompassing horizon of motion and time
- **A_1** — completed perception with dual residual trace: *resonant aisthēma* (formal-eidetic) + *resonant epithymia* (affective-orectic)
- **A_2** — the *phantasma* proper
- **A_3** — completed cognitive actuality: three orientational modes (intellection, memory, deliberative *phantasia bouleutikē*) + orthogonal committal *doxa*
- **A_4** — completed *praxis*

Each completed actuality is simultaneously terminus of its antecedent motion and unmoved originator of its successor.

§1.1 (Motion and Time as Horizon): *kinēsis* and *chronos* co-eternal (*Metaphysics* XII.6, 1071b6–11); motion as *energeia ateles* (*Physics* III.1, 201a10–14); Heidegger's *Bewegtheit* (BCAP §§25–26). Synchronic / diachronic dual register announced.

§1.2 (M_0 → A_1, Actualization of *Aisthēsis*): *aisthēsis* IS a *kinēsis* (*De Anima* II.5, 416b33–417a1); three-factor schema of *De Anima* III.10, 433b13–18 applies directly; hylomorphic reception (*De Anima* II.12, 424a17–24); one-in-substrate-different-in-being. Coining of *resonant kinēsis* + dual-resonance thesis (one residue, two beings: *resonant aisthēma* + *resonant epithymia*).

§1.3 (A_3, Completed Cognitive Actuality): A_3 = four-dimensional cognitive achievement converging on the *phantasma* stabilized at A_2. Three orientational modes (intellection / memory / discursive). *Doxa* enters as orthogonal committal dimension (involuntary, *logos*-dependent, exclusive to rational beings). Settled *doxai* as species of *hexis* (*Categories* 8, 8b25–9a13) function as additional unmoved originators feeding M_2 → A_3.

§1.4 (Emotion as Form of Desire Under Evaluative Disclosure): higher-order *pathē* (anger, fear, pity, shame from *Rhetoric* II) and basic *resonant epithymia* are two articulational concretions of one ontological structure (preservative *paschein* / *sōtēria*, *De Anima* II.5, 417b2–7). The doxa-gate: bare *phantasma* leaves the soul "unaffected" of higher-order *pathē*; *doxa* propositionally ratifies the *phantasma*, producing the higher-order *pathē* *euthys* (*De Anima* III.3, 427b21–24). The *pathetic* loop has two registers: synchronic + diachronic. *Hexis* bivalence (BCAP §17): *technē*-hexis (training reduces deliberation toward transparent routine) vs *praxis*-hexis (holding-oneself-open for fresh *kairos*-resolution).

§1.5 closes Chapter 1: integrative work, typology delivery, loop articulation, chapter synthesis.

================================================================
DISSERTATION COINAGES (italicized as units; deploy consistently)
================================================================

- ***resonant kinēsis*** — residual motion in the sensory apparatus persisting after object-withdrawal
- ***resonant aisthēma*** — formal-eidetic aspect of the residual motion
- ***resonant epithymia*** — affective-orectic aspect; basic-orectic-charge residue at A_1
- ***pathetic* loop** — judgement-modifying recursive structure of pathos (RETIRED: "pathos feedback loop")
- **articulational concretion** — axis along which generic *pathos* becomes determinate higher-order *pathē*
- **dual-resonance thesis** — A_1 deposits both formal-eidetic and affective-orectic residues simultaneously (RETIRED: "dual-trace")
- **content-conditional doxa-gate** — rule that *doxa* alone is necessary but not sufficient for higher-order *pathē*; the *doxa*'s content must engage evaluatively complex categories
- **synchronic / diachronic register** — synchronic = single chain-pass within one event; diachronic = cumulative trajectory reshaping dispositional ground
- ***technē*-hexis** / ***praxis*-hexis** — Heidegger's BCAP §17 bivalent reading of *hexis*
- **affective architecture of being-in-the-world** — closing synthesis term for emotion's ontological function

Greek faculty-names (preferred over English): *aisthētikon*, *aisthētērion*, *orektikon*, *kritikon*, *kinētikon*, *phantastikon*.

Aristotle work titles use Latin/Greek standard form: *De Anima* (NEVER *On the Soul*); *De Motu Animalium* (NEVER *Movement of Animals*); *De Insomniis* (NEVER *On Dreams*); *De Memoria* (NEVER *On Memory*); *De Sensu* (NEVER *Sense and Sensibilia*).

Heideggerian German (untranslated): *Bewegtheit*, *Befindlichkeit* (NOT "state-of-mind"; "disposedness" — Kisiel), *Stimmung* (NOT "mood" in ontological-atmospheric register; "attunement" — Rickert), *Sorge*, *Geworfenheit*, *Geschichtlichkeit*, *Zeitlichkeit*, *Ekstasen*, *Gewesenheit*, *Gegenwart*, *Zukunft*, *Mitsein*, *Augenblick*, Dasein.

**De Motu Animalium 7, 701a29–b1** (Subsection 4 Type 1 load-bearing block-quote):
> "And so what we do without reflection, we do quickly. For when a man is actually using perception or imagination or thought in relation to that for the sake of which, what he desires he does at once. For the actualizing of desire is a substitute for inquiry or thinking. I want to drink, says appetite; this is drink, says sense or imagination or thought: straightaway I drink. In this way living creatures are impelled to move and to act, and desire is the last cause of movement, and desire arises through perception or through imagination and thought. And things that desire to act make and act sometimes from appetite or impulse and sometimes from wish."

**De Motu Animalium 7, 701a7–16** (Subsection 4 Type 2 load-bearing block-quote):
> "But how is it that thought is sometimes followed by action, sometimes not; sometimes by movement, sometimes not? What happens seems parallel to the case of thinking and inferring about the immovable objects. There the end is the truth seen (for, when one thinks the two propositions, one thinks and puts together the conclusion), but here the two propositions result in a conclusion which is an action---for example, whenever one thinks that every man ought to walk, and that one is a man oneself, straightaway one walks; or that, in this case, no man should walk, one is a man: straightaway one remains at rest. And one so acts in the two cases provided that there is nothing to compel or to prevent."

All movement involves three factors, (1) that which originates the movement, (2) that by means of which it originates it, and (3) that which is moved. The expression 'that which originates the movement' is ambiguous: it may mean either something which itself is unmoved or that which at once moves and is moved. Here that which moves without itself being moved is the realizable good, that which at once moves and is moved is the faculty of appetite (for that which is moved is moved insofar as it desires, and appetite in the sense of actual appetite *is* a kind of movement)."

SUBSECTION 6 of 9 — *Hexis* Bivalence: *Technē*-Hexis and *Praxis*-Hexis
================================================================

(The CLI invocation passes the LaTeX heading, word target ~900, quotation count 2 (the two BCAP block-quotes), and output format via subsection-mode flags. This delta supplies the topical content + dissertation-specific deployment guidance.)

**Subsection role.** Develop the *hexis* dimension that §1.4 set up at L195–201.

Open with *Categories* 8, 8b25–9a13: *hexis* is a settled disposition, more stable than *diathesis*, encompassing virtues, crafts, knowledge, and bodily states. State that settled *doxai* are ONE SPECIES of *hexis* (the doxastic-cognitive species; warrant: *De Motu Animalium* 7, 701a7–16, where the practical syllogism's universal premise is a settled *doxa*) but that *hexis* is the broader genus. Reference *Metaphysics* Δ.20, 1022b4 (*hexis* as activity of haver and had) and *Nicomachean Ethics* II.1, 1103a14–b25 (moral excellence comes about as a result of habit) for the broader doctrine.

Then deploy Heidegger's bivalent reading from BCAP §17. The two block-quotes are load-bearing.

**Technē-hexis block-quote (BCAP p. 127).** Use `\begin{adjustwidth}{0.5in}{0in}` ... `\end{adjustwidth}` markup. Verbatim text from Source B:

> "Through practice, by frequently-undergoing, it comes about that being-oriented puts the prescription further and further out of play. Training has the precise sense of reducing deliberation insofar as it is through training that the completedness of attaining a result comes about."

Develop the structural reading: training reduces deliberation; the *technē*-grounded *doxa* runs the chain WITHOUT engaging higher-order *pathē*. The expert pianist's hands, the carpenter's chisel-grip, the orator's settled cadence — each is a *technē*-hexis that fires the Type 2 chain through transparent procedural *doxa*. The "completedness of attaining a result" is the *technē*-hexis's defining ergonomic structure: the result is external, the operation is means-to-end, and training is the cultivation of routine.

**Praxis-hexis block-quote (BCAP p. 128).** Use `\begin{adjustwidth}{0.5in}{0in}` ... `\end{adjustwidth}` markup. Verbatim text from Source B:

> "Cultivating *hexis* never depends on an operation, a routine. In an operation, the moment is destroyed. Every completedness, as settled routine, breaks down in the face of the moment. Appropriation and cultivation of *hexis* through habituation means nothing other than correct repetition.... The distinction lies in the fact that *praxis* depends on the *how*. The how is only appropriated in such a way that the human being enables himself *to be composed at each moment*; not routine but holding-oneself-open, *dynamis* in the *mesotēs*."

Develop the structural reading: *praxis*-hexis is holding-oneself-open for fresh *kairos*-resolution; it is the *hexis* through which an agent enters Type 3 evaluatively complex action well — neither bypassing *doxa* (Type 1) nor running it on routine (Type 2). The "moment" (*Augenblick*, in Heidegger's later vocabulary) is precisely what *technē*-hexis destroys and what *praxis*-hexis sustains.

Connect *praxis*-hexis to *phronēsis* (*Nicomachean Ethics* VI.5, 1140a24–b30: "a true and reasoned state of capacity to act with regard to the things that are good or bad for man") — *phronēsis* is the canonical practical-rational *hexis* that exemplifies *praxis*-hexis's holding-oneself-open structure.

Connect *technē*-hexis to BCAP pp. 122–123 ("for there is no *technē* for the *kairos*") — the *kairos* is precisely what *technē*-hexis cannot resolve; it requires *praxis*-hexis.

**Mapping onto the three types.** Map the bivalence onto the three types:

- Type 1 (Simple appetition) bypasses both *technē*-hexis and *praxis*-hexis: it is appetitive-immediate.
- Type 2 (Habitual-rational) routes through *technē*-hexis: settled procedural *doxa* fires without evaluative engagement.
- Type 3 (Evaluatively complex) routes through *praxis*-hexis: the agent enters fresh evaluative resolution under cultivated dispositional readiness.

Note that *praxis*-hexis uniquely exercises a two-level reach: it modulates BOTH the basic-valence input at A_1 (the *Stimmung*-saturation of perceptual disclosure) AND the doxa-gate at A_2 → A_3 (the corrective faculty's preparation for fresh evaluative ratification). *Technē*-hexis, by contrast, runs the chain forward without engaging the evaluative axis at all.

**Optional Gross deployment.** If natural for the dispositional-bodily dimension, deploy *Gross, "Introduction" in Heidegger and Rhetoric (2005), p. 26* (enmattered-*eidos* thesis) here — the body's condition is essential to the *eidos* of fear, and *praxis*-hexis is the cultivation through which the body's dispositional condition becomes ready for fresh evaluative resolution. Quote verbatim from Source E (do NOT paraphrase).

**Closing.** Close with the diachronic claim: every completed action at A_4 sediments back into the agent's *hexeis*, but the kind of *hexis* sedimented depends on which type of action was completed (Type 2 deepens *technē*-hexis; Type 3 deepens *praxis*-hexis). This sets up §7's analysis of the *pathetic* loop.
